skill.name: quick-quality-check
skill.description: Run a fast parallel quality check across theater detection, style, security, tests, and token usage for a target path.
skill.summary: Run fast parallel code quality checks with severity-ranked results.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code fence or inline-code false positives. One real command-execution concern remains in the Bash execution flow, where external tools run against an interpolated path. Additional review should address shell quoting and unpinned npx execution before publication.

remediation.issue: User path is interpolated into shell command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Validate paths against the workspace, reject shell metacharacters, and pass paths as structured arguments instead of embedded shell strings.

remediation.issue: npx claude-flow commands are not pinned to a version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions or require a vetted local installation before running these commands.

remediation.issue: The skill can run several external tools in parallel.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and document all required tools before command execution.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Path In Shell Commands
semantic_findings.description: The execution flow places the required path input into shell command strings executed through GNU parallel. A crafted path containing quotes or shell metacharacters could change the command that runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly defines a user-supplied path and later expands it inside parallel shell command strings. The exact runtime wrapper is not shown, so the injection risk is strong but not certain.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned npx Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The execution flow runs npx claude-flow commands without a pinned version or trusted local dependency. This can execute unexpected package versions if the package source changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple npx claude-flow commands are shown without version pins or integrity guidance. This is a common supply-chain risk, although no malicious package source is specified.

content.value_statement: Quick code reviews often miss security, style, test, and placeholder issues. This skill runs parallel checks and returns a severity-ranked quality report.
actual_capabilities: Defines an input contract for checking a file or directory path.
Runs theater detection, style audit, security scan, test coverage, and token usage checks.
Initializes a claude-flow swarm and specialized quality agent for parallel work.
Aggregates separate check outputs into a unified quality report.
Ranks issues by severity and reports a quality score.
limitations: Requires claude-flow, GNU parallel, jq, and related command-line tools.
The sample commands need careful path validation and shell quoting.
Quick mode can miss complex defects that require deeper analysis.
The skill does not define automatic fixes for reported issues.

The summary recommends deeper audit because quick checks found high-risk security and coverage gaps.

best_practices: Confirm all required CLI tools are installed before running the skill.
Use trusted local paths and validate paths before shell execution.
Review security findings manually before merging or publishing.
anti_patterns: Running checks on untrusted path values without validation.
Treating a quick score as a complete security review.
Ignoring failed checks because other parallel checks succeeded.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code?
faq.answer: The skill describes checks and report aggregation. It does not define automatic code changes.

faq.question: Which tools does it require?
faq.answer: It expects claude-flow, GNU parallel, jq, and a shell environment that can run the shown commands.

faq.question: Can it replace a deep audit?
faq.answer: No. It is a quick feedback tool and may miss complex security or architecture issues.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review commands first and avoid running external tools on untrusted paths without isolation.

faq.question: What is theater detection?
faq.answer: It looks for mocks, TODOs, placeholders, and other signs that code may not be production ready.

faq.question: How should failed checks be handled?
faq.answer: Keep independent checks running, then escalate high or critical issues to detailed review.
